description: Junior engineer level (1 to 3 years professional experience). Focuses on practical day-to-day software development, clean implementation, testing, debugging, and understanding basic design patterns within existing codebases.

axes.depth: Practical familiarity with language idioms, testing frameworks, standard APIs, database queries, and basic error handling.
axes.ambiguity: Moderate ambiguity; questions may require identifying typical missing requirements or common operational failure modes.
axes.expectedScope: Feature-level implementation, component architecture, API endpoints, bug triage, and small subsystem contributions.
axes.followUpPressure: Moderate follow-ups on testing edge cases, boundary conditions, failure scenarios, and code maintainability.
axes.behavioralExpectations: Demonstrates team collaboration, responsiveness to code reviews, proactive communication when blocked, and reliable execution.

relevance.name: Relevance & Directness
relevance.description: Directly tackles practical engineering challenges and frames answers around practical production considerations.

anchors.1: Drifts into theoretical tangents without providing a practical software implementation or answer to the problem.
anchors.3: Provides a sensible, working practical solution that addresses the user story or technical requirement directly.
anchors.5: Delivers an exact, pragmatic solution; immediately addresses requirements and highlights relevant production edge cases.

structure.name: Structural Framing
structure.description: Presents structured workflows: requirement understanding -> design approach -> edge case handling -> verification.

anchors.1: Jumps straight to implementation details without clarifying requirements, testing strategy, or context.
anchors.3: Presents a clear structure: clarifies the goal, describes the implementation, and discusses how to test it.
anchors.5: Very disciplined delivery: frames context efficiently, highlights trade-offs systematically, and closes with verification results.

depth.name: Technical & Conceptual Depth
depth.description: Demonstrates practical software development expertise including error handling, testing, and concurrency basics.

anchors.1: Ignores errors, null checks, race conditions, or performance implications in typical software environments.
anchors.3: Considers validation, basic error recovery, unit testing, and common runtime behaviors accurately.
anchors.5: Shows strong practical depth: discusses idempotent retries, database transaction boundaries, or profiling tools thoughtfully.

clarity.name: Clarity & Articulation
clarity.description: Communicates engineering concepts with accurate terminology and clear, professional delivery.

anchors.1: Imprecise terminology, rambling explanations, or difficulty articulating why a specific library or method was chosen.
anchors.3: Uses standard engineering terminology accurately and explains logic in a straightforward, listener-friendly manner.
anchors.5: Exceptionally clear and professional communication; conveys complex bugs and resolutions with brevity and confidence.

levelFit.name: Level Alignment
levelFit.description: Calibrated against 1-3 year engineering expectations for feature delivery and professional execution.

anchors.1: Lacks basic awareness of professional software practices such as automated testing, git workflows, or code reviews.
anchors.3: Solid junior engineer: delivers dependable code, understands basic design patterns, and collaborates productively with teammates.
anchors.5: Exhibits near-mid-level maturity: demonstrates self-directed debugging, proactive test coverage, and clean modular designs.
